key_insight: Task-dependent model choice mattered: GPT-5.5 was best for medication/entity detection, while fine-tuned local Qwen models performed better for normalized record assembly and laboratory tuple extraction.
clinical_relevance: For multilingual stroke discharge summaries, local models may be enough for some structured extraction tasks, potentially reducing reliance on cloud inference when building clinical NLP workflows.
method: Retrospective system evaluation on multilingual, non-English stroke discharge summaries
Compared multilingual encoders, locally fine-tuned Qwen3-4B models, and zero-shot GPT-5.5
Measured section extraction, medication extraction/normalization, and laboratory record recovery
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 332 section cases, 149 medication cases with 2,475 reference records, and 191 laboratory cases; corpus-wide extraction covered 193,101 summaries and 13.3 H100 GPU-hours.
watch_item: Performance depended on annotation conventions, normalization rules, and section extraction quality, so results may not generalize without local validation and workflow-specific tuning.
paper_title: Task-dependent model selection for structured extraction from multilingual non-English clinical records
